items.finding: The source notes that Raman spectroscopy is frequently applied in upstream processing due to its high selectivity and low water interference.
items.how_it_applies: This suggests testing Raman probes for monitoring metabolic changes to see if low water interference helps track components effectively during fermentation.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The finding stems from general biopharmaceutical reviews rather than yeast fermentation specifically, and conditions at scale may differ from laboratory findings.
